classification.difficultyReason: Development: students measure four divided-bar segments and connect each measured share of the 10 cm whole to a visitor frequency. This links measurement and proportional interpretation using the taught whole-times-share method, without requiring an unfamiliar inference.

content.prompt: This bar represents the $500\,000$ visitors to the Royal Easter Show in Sydney. The bar is $10\text{ cm}$ long. Using a ruler, estimate how many people visited during which times.

spec.description: Centred horizontal category bar. Labels sit near the upper-left of each segment. The bar coordinate frame is exactly 100 mm wide, excluding label bounds and padding. No ticks, scale labels or legend. Printed measurement correction: the drawn bar spans exactly 100 mm. The SVG frame is 102.17153395369128 mm to accommodate 0.5 mm geometric padding per side and the compiler’s leading space; the frame is not the measurement target.
spec.mathematics: Total 500000 visitors; bar length 100 mm; segment lengths 40, 15, 20 and 25 mm from left to right. These are reconstruction dimensions, not printed numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Category labels and coloured segments are student-visible givens. Measurements and visitor estimates appear only in answers.

answer.short: All day: approximately ${200\,000}$; AM only: approximately ${75\,000}$; PM only: approximately ${100\,000}$; evening only: approximately ${125\,000}$ visitors.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Visitors per centimetre}&=500\,000\div10\\&=50\,000\end{align*}$$
The measured lengths are approximately $4\text{ cm}$, $1.5\text{ cm}$, $2\text{ cm}$ and $2.5\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{All day visitors}&\approx4\times50\,000=200\,000\\\text{AM only visitors}&\approx1.5\times50\,000=75\,000\\\text{PM only visitors}&\approx2\times50\,000=100\,000\\\text{Evening only visitors}&\approx2.5\times50\,000=125\,000\end{align*}$$
